Q: Delete key and pair from Json file A:

Much easier, you can use the _delitem_ function in order to remove items you want. For example:

dic = [key1, key2, key3, key4]
del_items = ['key1', 'Key2']
for i in del_item:
  dic.__delitem__(i)

print(dic)

Result: [key3, key4]

Q: Remove extra space between paired values A:

You need to use scale_x_continuous() and set the labels manually. We can wrap the labels so they take less space. You can also change the width of position_dodge. And finally, save your plot to a file to control the dimensions.

library(ggplot2)
library(sjPlot)
library(lme4)

model27 <- lmer(Time ~ Demonstrator * Shelter + (1 | Subject), data = dat)

m27 <- plot_model(model27, type = "pred", terms = c("Demonstrator", "Shelter"),
                  title = "Predicted Time in Shelters",
                  axis.title = c("", "Time Spent In Shelter"))

m27$layers[[1]]$position <- position_dodge(width = 0.3)
m27$layers[[2]]$position <- position_dodge(width = 0.3)

p <- m27 +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Shelter Type",
    labels = c("Demonstrated", "Non Demonstrated"),
    values = c("blue", "red")
    ) +
   scale_x_continuous(
     expand = expansion(mult = -1),
     breaks = 1:3,
     labels = gsub(" ", "\n", levels(dat$Demonstrator))
   ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14)
    )

ggsave("plot.png", plot = p, width = 6, height = 6)

Sample data:

set.seed(123)
dat <- data.frame(
  Time = c(rnorm(20, 3.75, 0.5), rnorm(20, 3.7, 0.5),
           rnorm(20, 3.8, 0.8), rnorm(20, 3.65, 0.8),
           rnorm(20, 3.2, 0.9), rnorm(20, 3.5, 0.7)),
  Demonstrator = factor(rep(c("Dom Female", "High Sub Female", "Low Sub Male"), 
                            each = 40)),
  Shelter = factor(rep(rep(c("Demonstrated", "Non Demonstrated"), 
                           each = 20), 3)),
  Subject = factor(rep(1:20, each = 6))
)

Q: Nested dict with parent/child relation A:

EDIT:
As @deceze noticed in comment: "This will fail if a child appears before its parent in the list."
So this method has some restriction.
But function find_parent() still can be useful to find person when you have all data in dictionary.

I used separate function which uses recursion to find parent in new list.

def find_parent(name, data):
    # print("find_parent:", name, data)
    for item in data:
        if item["name"] == name:
            return item
        elif "child" in item:
            return find_parent(name, item["child"])
    # return None

# ---

data = [{"name": "a"}, {"name": "b", "parent": "a"}, {"name": "c", "parent": "b"}]

result = []

for item in data:
    if "parent" not in item:
        result.append(item.copy())
        # print("name: ", item["name"], "| parent: - without parent -")
    else:
        parent = find_parent(item["parent"], result)
        # print("name: ", item["name"], "| parent:", parent)
        if parent:
            if "child" not in parent:
                parent["child"] = []
            parent["child"].append(item.copy())
        else:
            print("Can't find parent:", item["parent"])

# ---

print(result)

And version which uses another dict to keep persons as {name:reference_to_item_in_new_list} and it doesn't need recurency.

data = [{"name": "a"}, {"name": "b", "parent": "a"}, {"name": "c", "parent": "b"}]

result = []

persons = {}  # another dict for 

for item in data:
    if "parent" not in item:
        item = item.copy()
        result.append(item)
        persons[item["name"]] = item
    else:
        parent = persons.get(item["parent"])
        if parent:
            if "child" not in parent:
                parent["child"] = []
            item = item.copy()
            parent["child"].append(item)
            persons[item["name"]] = item
        else:
            print("Can't find parent:", item["parent"])

# ---

print(result)

Q: Detect column resize in Tkinter treeview A:

Thanks to @Thingamabobs. Basically, I have to save the id of the created widget on the canvas and when there is a move event, if it is the separator, then the relative movement of the separator object is done.

The modifications:

  1. Add a few more columns to the header table

    HDR_TAG = 0; HDR_NAME = 1; HDR_WIDTH = 2 ; HDR_ANCHOR = 3; HDR_SEP = 4; HDR_X = 5; HDR_Y = 6

  2. In initUI, extra columns were added. The tuples had to be changed to lists so that they could be modified

            self.headers = [
            ['#0', 'Name', 100, tk.W, None, 0, 0],
            ['upper', 'Upper', 60, tk.E, None, 0, 0],
            ['lower', 'Lower', 60, tk.CENTER, None, 0, 0]
        ]

  3. In initOverlay, the ids of the vertical separators were saved

           # Now do the verticals
        x = 0
        ybeg = int(hstep)
        yhgt = hgt - ybeg
        for col in self.headers:
            x += col[HDR_WIDTH]
            sep = ttk.Separator(self.parent, orient=tk.VERTICAL)
            col[HDR_X] = x
            col[HDR_Y] = ybeg
            col[HDR_SEP] = self.canvas.create_window((x, ybeg), height=yhgt, window=sep, anchor='nw')

  4. In initUI, two new bindings were added

            # Set up resize events
        self.tree.bind('<B1-Motion>', self.resize_check)
        self.tree.bind('<ButtonRelease-1>', self.resize_end)

  5. Code for the resizing

        def resize_check(self, event):
        tree = event.widget
        if tree.identify_region(event.x, event.y) == 'separator':
            self.resize_column()
            self.resizing = True
        elif self.resizing:
            self.resize_column()

    def resize_end(self, event):
        self.resizing = False

    def resize_column(self):
        # Get the new sizes
        x = 0
        for col in self.headers:
            col[HDR_WIDTH] = self.tree.column(col[HDR_TAG], 'width')
            x += col[HDR_WIDTH]
            if col[HDR_SEP] != None and col[HDR_X] != x:
                self.canvas.move(col[HDR_SEP], x - col[HDR_X], 0)
                col[HDR_X] = x

And that's it - it just works.

I'll have to try it using place instead of the canvas.
